key_insight: State-of-the-art VLMs can generate fluent diagnostic text but often fail simple pre-diagnostic sanity checks (modality, anatomy, view/orientation, image integrity), exposing a "Medical Moravec's Paradox": models are better at high-level language than basic visual validation.
problem_solved: Addresses the missing evaluation and failure modes around pre-diagnostic sanity checking in medical VLMs by introducing a clinical triage perspective and benchmark to reveal when inputs are unsafe or unreadable for diagnosis.
method: Construct a clinical triage benchmark that explicitly tests pre-diagnostic sanity checks (correct imaging modality, relevant anatomy, plausible viewpoint/orientation, and image integrity).
Systematically evaluate multiple VLMs on these triage tests using standardized metrics to quantify failure modes and expose vulnerabilities.
Analyze errors and propose a triage-first evaluation/deployment pipeline and practical recommendations to force or verify visual validity before diagnostic inference.
impact: Highlights a critical safety gap in medical VLM deployment: ensuring basic visual validity before trusting diagnostic outputs. Encourages practitioners to adopt triage-first benchmarks, safer pipelines, and improved model evaluation criteria.
visual_elements: Flowchart showing 'Input image → Clinical triage checks (modality, anatomy, view, integrity) → Pass/fail → Diagnostic model' to illustrate the proposed pipeline.
Bar chart comparing multiple VLMs' accuracy on each sanity-check category (modality, anatomy, view, integrity).
Annotated failure-case examples (image + model output) demonstrating common hallucinations or misreads when triage fails.
Heatmap or matrix of error types across models to visualize concentrated weaknesses (e.g., view confusion vs. anatomy misclassification).
paper_title: MedObvious: Exposing the Medical Moravec's Paradox in VLMs via Clinical Triage
paper_authors: Ufaq Khan, Umair Nawaz, L D M S S Teja, Numaan Saeed, Muhammad Bilal
